status: EXPLORATORY — does not modify or replace the pre-registered 137-trade baseline
description: Pre-registration for the pledged-collateral overlay study. Written and committed before any analysis code for this experiment is written or run. No number has been computed at the time this file is created.
research_question: If the margin for this strangle were funded by pledging an existing long-term equity holding rather than by fresh cash, would the overlay ever have forced a sale of those pledged shares -- and how much cash must sit idle for it not to?
framing: Pledging does not change the strategy's P&L by a single point. It changes capital efficiency and it changes what is at risk. This study measures the tail-risk price of that capital efficiency. It is not a study of whether the strangle is profitable -- that question is already answered elsewhere in this project and this study may not claim credit for it.

primary_source.document: SEBI Master Circular Chapter 4, "Comprehensive Risk Management for Cash Market and Debt Segment", December 2024

verified_facts.fact: Clearing members must maintain at least 50% of total collateral as cash or cash equivalents; SEBI states explicitly this requirement may NOT be applied at individual client level.

verified_facts.para: 1.1.2, liquid assets table, "Other Liquid Assets" note 1 and note iv
verified_facts.fact: Non-cash collateral CANNOT be used to meet mark-to-market losses; MTM must be met in cash or cash equivalents.
Equity shares as collateral carry a VaR-based haircut of 6 sigma, subject to a minimum of 9%. The haircut is dynamic and widens with volatility.
Total Other Liquid Assets may not exceed total Cash Equivalents.

secondary_facts_not_primary_verified.fact: Broker practice passes the 50/50 requirement through to clients despite fact 1 -- Zerodha states the clearing corporation requires the broker to fund any client cash shortfall; HDFC Securities charges daily interest on cash-component deficiency.
secondary_facts_not_primary_verified.source: Zerodha and HDFC Securities public statements (not independently fetched/cited by URL in this file)

secondary_facts_not_primary_verified.fact: Reported April 2026 tightening: brokers required to hold 50% of F&O margin in cash, and RBI reportedly raising equity collateral haircuts to 40%.
secondary_facts_not_primary_verified.status: SECONDARY, NOT VERIFIED against SEBI or RBI primary sources

collateral.description: A stylised NIFTY-tracking proxy. Fixed unit count purchased at 2024-01-04, value floats with the index thereafter.

position.sensitivity_only_note: Naked version is a labelled sensitivity only -- its margin is a flat 10%-of-notional approximation and no conclusion may rest on it.

margin.source: Recompute per trade from outputs/backtest_trades_137.csv using its real lot_size column. Do NOT reuse any rupee column from outputs/margin_return_analysis.csv.
margin.winged_margin_formula: (max spread width x lot size) - net credit at entry

haircut.sensitivity_40_note: Rests on unverified secondary source (fact 6) and must be labelled as such wherever reported.

cash_fraction.sensitivity_source: What the regulation literally permits at client level, primary-verified (fact 1)

model.available_margin_formula: A = C + min(U, C), where C = cash and U = haircut-adjusted collateral value. The min() term implements primary fact 4 (Other Liquid Assets may not exceed Cash Equivalents).

breach_types.type_2_cash_breach: Peak intraday MTM loss exceeds C. Follows from primary fact 2 (pledged shares cannot meet MTM).

peak_mtm_loss.reported_as: A RANGE, never a single number.
peak_mtm_loss.method_b_high_based_upper_bound: Using HghPric for both short legs from data/processed/nifty_expiry_day_chains.csv.
peak_mtm_loss.caveat_pre_registered: The call's high and the put's high need not occur simultaneously, so method (b) is a conservative upper bound on a path that may never have existed, not a measured worst moment.

primary_metric: LOCKED -- nothing else may be used to judge the result: whether any Type 1 or Type 2 breach occurs across the 137 trades, and the size in rupees of the worst shortfall of each type.
secondary_metrics: Minimum coverage ratio across the sample.
Return on the cash actually posted.

pre_registered_rule_departure.departure: This study reports in RUPEES, not points, departing from the project's standing points-primary rule.
pre_registered_rule_departure.justification: Collateral value, haircuts and cash buffers are inherently rupee quantities with no points equivalent.
pre_registered_rule_departure.mitigation: All margin figures use real per-trade lot size from backtest_trades_137.csv, never a flat assumption, so the rupee figures remain internally consistent across all four lot-size regimes.

claim_A_same_day_margin_relief.reasoning: Newly purchased shares settle T+1 and require further pledge processing, so they cannot meet a same-day margin or MTM call.
claim_A_same_day_margin_relief.treatment: Documented as a mechanism, not tested numerically.

claim_B_cost_basis.funding_source: Crash-day purchases funded from a ring-fenced cash pot held SEPARATELY from the margin cash C, so the two uses of cash are never double-counted.
claim_B_cost_basis.caveat_pre_registered: If this ring-fenced cash exists, it could have been posted as margin instead -- the proposal is partly self-cancelling and the write-up must say so.

crash_threshold.definition: X = the 95th-percentile adverse open-to-close move in data/raw/nifty50_daily.csv over 2016-01-01 to 2023-12-31.
crash_threshold.rationale: This period is deliberately OUTSIDE the 2024+ window being tested, so the threshold cannot be tuned to the trades it judges.
crash_threshold.computation_timing: Compute X in the analysis phase, not now.

out_of_sample_stress_case.note: NOT an expiry day and NOT one of the 137 baseline trades. Report it separately as a stress scenario, never pooled with the 137-trade results.

predictions.statement: Type 2 (cash) breaches will occur more often than Type 1 (margin) breaches.
At base-case parameters, at least one breach of some type occurs across the 137 trades.
The high-based peak-MTM measure produces at least twice as many breaches as the close-based measure.
Beta 1.3 produces more breaches than beta 0.7.
The 2024-06-04 stress scenario breaches at base-case parameters.

reporting_rule: Report pass/fail honestly for each prediction in the analysis phase; do not soften a failure.
protected_files_note: This study must never modify src/margin_return_analysis.py or outputs/margin_return_analysis.csv. That file's flat LOT_SIZE=65 is a known, accepted, documented inconsistency and is out of scope for this study -- this study computes its own margin figures independently from outputs/backtest_trades_137.csv instead of reusing that file's numbers.
